title: Tanya's W-2 uploaded twice (PDF + phone photo)
trap: Autoflow picks up both documents -> $47,000 wages and $2,810 withholding counted twice.
correct_treatment: Mark photo upload as DUP (same EIN, control no., amounts). One W-2 for Brightsmile Dental.

procedure_section: General Return Prep Notes - blank organizer line with PY amount
title: Ally Bank 1099-INT not in initial PBC
trap: Organizer line blank; preparer assumes zero and omits $1,246 of interest (recurring, $980 in 2024).
correct_treatment: Open item emailed to client 02/24; 1099-INT received 03/04 and included on line 2b.

title: Newborn not on organizer
trap: Organizer lists 2 dependents; baby born 12/18/2025 only disclosed in a later email.
correct_treatment: Add Noah as dependent (child born during the year is treated as living with the taxpayer all year; SSN issued before due date). Third $2,200 CTC.

procedure_section: OBBBA - no tax on overtime (Schedule 1-A Part III)
title: W-2 box 14 shows TOTAL overtime pay
trap: Deduct the full $9,450 box 14 overtime amount.
correct_treatment: Only the FLSA premium ('half' of time-and-a-half) qualifies. Box 14 = total OT paid at 1.5x -> premium = 9,450 / 3 = $3,150.

procedure_section: OBBBA - car loan interest (Schedule 1-A Part IV)
title: Two vehicle loans, only one qualifies
trap: Deduct both loans ($3,557) or neither.
correct_treatment: F-150: new, 2025 purchase, US final assembly, personal use, VIN reported -> $2,452 deductible. CR-V: used vehicle, 2024 loan -> not qualified.

title: Dependent care FSA and overnight camp
trap: Claim credit on $6,000 of expenses ignoring the $5,000 W-2 box 10 exclusion and including overnight camp.
correct_treatment: Exclude $5,000 FSA (box 10) first; credit base = $6,000 cap - $5,000 = $1,000; overnight camp ($1,400) is not a qualified expense. Credit 20% x $1,000 = $200.

title: HSA code W includes employee pre-tax payroll deferrals
trap: Take an additional HSA deduction on Schedule 1 line 13 for the $2,000 Marcus 'contributed'.
correct_treatment: Code W = employer + cafeteria-plan contributions, already excluded from wages. No Sch 1 deduction. 1099-SA used for qualified medical - nontaxable; Form 8889 still required.

title: Roth 401(k) (code AA) is not pre-tax
trap: Subtract $2,600 code AA from wages.
correct_treatment: Code AA is already included in box 1. No adjustment.

title: Organizer says 'Single' but client qualifies for HOH
trap: Carry forward the organizer / PY filing status (Single, no dependent) - standard deduction $15,750, Single brackets, no EIC/CTC.
correct_treatment: Unmarried, paid > 1/2 the cost of keeping up the home, qualifying child (son, 7) lived with her > 1/2 the year -> Head of household: standard deduction $23,625, HOH brackets; claim Arjun as dependent.
impact: Refund $5,141 vs balance due $361 on a naive Single/no-dependent return

procedure_section: Post-Submission Exceptions - E-File Rejects / Paper Filing Returns
title: Child's father also claims the child -> IND-507-01 reject
trap: Remove Arjun (or switch back to Single) to get the e-file accepted because 'dad claims him every year'.
correct_treatment: Priya is the custodial parent (child lived with her the greater number of nights), no Form 8332 / written release signed, so only she may claim Arjun (dependency, CTC, EIC, HOH). Document the reject, paper-file the same return with the school/lease support retained; IRS will resolve the duplicate with the father (CP87A).

title: 1099-K for personal items sold at a loss
trap: Treat PayPal 1099-K gross $6,812 as Schedule C gross receipts (SE tax) or other income, or ignore it (CP2000 risk).
correct_treatment: Personal-use property sold below cost is not income and the loss is not deductible. Report $6,812 on Schedule 1 line 8z and the same amount on line 24z ('Form 1099-K personal items sold at a loss') so the 1099-K is matched and AGI is unaffected.
impact: Avoids $6,812 of phantom income (+ SE tax) and preserves EIC

procedure_section: Return - Schedule A (state refunds of taxes previously itemized)
title: 1099-G IL refund $212
trap: Include the $212 state refund on Schedule 1 line 1.
correct_treatment: 2024 return used the standard deduction -> no tax benefit from the IL tax -> refund not taxable (tax benefit rule). Not reported.

title: Lifetime Learning Credit - qualified expenses
trap: Add the $850 laptop to the 1098-T tuition, or skip the credit because box 8 (half-time) is unchecked.
correct_treatment: LLC has no half-time requirement (one course is enough). Qualified expenses = tuition & fees paid to the school $2,388; the laptop was not required to be purchased from the institution -> not qualified for LLC. LLC = 20% = $478.

title: Saver's credit missed / ordered after CTC
trap: Ignore Form 8880 (401k deferrals code D) or apply it after the CTC so it is wiped out.
correct_treatment: Part-time student (not full-time) with $2,496 elective deferrals and AGI $36,463 (HOH 20% tier) -> saver's credit $400. It is subtracted before the CTC on Credit Limit Worksheet A, so more of the $2,200 CTC becomes refundable ACTC ($1,700, capped at $1,700).

procedure_section: Return - Schedule B (federal obligations exempt at state level)
title: TreasuryDirect interest
trap: Treat I-bond/T-bill interest as tax-exempt federally, or forget the IL subtraction; also the organizer line was blank.
correct_treatment: Box 3 interest is taxable federally (line 2b); subtract $310 on IL Schedule M (U.S. obligations). The duplicate 'REPRINT' 1099-INT is the same form - count once.

title: IL EIC and IL child tax credit
trap: Stop at IL tax less withholding; miss the refundable IL EIC (20% of federal) and IL child tax credit; or claim the K-12 education expense credit for $165 of school fees.
correct_treatment: IL EIC $446 + IL child tax credit $178 (assumed 40% of IL EIC for 2025); school fees are below the $250 floor for the K-12 credit.

title: Allocated tips (W-2 box 8) vs actual tip diary
trap: Add W-2 box 8 allocated tips $2,900 to wages (line 1c) and Form 4137, or ignore unreported tips entirely.
correct_treatment: Allocated tips are not in box 1. With adequate daily records (contemporaneous tip diary) the taxpayer reports ACTUAL unreported tips - $1,600 - on line 1c and Form 4137 instead of the $2,900 allocation. Document the judgment in the WP.

title: SS/Medicare on unreported tips
trap: Report the $1,600 as wages without Form 4137 (no FICA) or compute SE tax on it.
correct_treatment: Form 4137: 6.2% + 1.45% on $1,600 = $122 on Schedule 2 line 5; tips also count toward the SS wage base on Schedule SE line 8b.

procedure_section: Scan - Unstructured PBC (Schedule C records / handwritten mileage log)
title: Commuting miles in the mileage log
trap: Use the client's 19,325 'total biz' miles (includes 4,180 miles driving to the casino bartending job).
correct_treatment: Driving between home and the W-2 job is commuting. Business miles = Uber online miles 15,145 x $0.70 = $10,602 + tolls.

procedure_section: Return - Schedule C (1099-K gross vs net)
title: Rideshare 1099-K gross includes Uber fees and tips
trap: Report net deposits ($28,730) as gross receipts, or report the 1099-K gross without deducting the Uber service/booking fees; or omit the 1099-NEC incentives / count the duplicate 1099-K twice.
correct_treatment: Gross receipts = 1099-K $38,720 + 1099-NEC $1,150 = $39,870; deduct Uber service fee, booking and airport fees ($11,140) on line 10. Second 1099-K upload is a duplicate.

procedure_section: Return - OBBBA no tax on tips (Schedule 1-A Part II)
title: Qualified tips from W-2, 4137 and Schedule C
trap: Deduct only W-2 box 7 (or include allocated tips), and exceed the $25,000 cap.
correct_treatment: Qualified tips = box 7 $24,600 + Form 4137 $1,600 + rider tips $2,860 (rideshare driver is a listed occupation; SE tips limited to Schedule C net) = $29,060, capped at $25,000. Unreported allocated tips never qualify.

title: Actual car costs claimed on top of standard mileage
trap: Deduct gas, insurance and oil changes from the organizer in addition to 70 cents/mile.
correct_treatment: Standard mileage rate replaces operating costs (gas, insurance, maintenance, depreciation); only tolls/parking added. Standard mileage was elected in the first business-use year (2024), so it may continue.

title: SE tax and QBI on rideshare profit
trap: Skip SE tax because the W-2 already has FICA, or compute QBI on net profit without the 1/2 SE tax reduction.
correct_treatment: SE tax on $16,647 x 92.35% = $2,352 (SS base not reached); QBI = net - 1/2 SE = $15,471 -> $3,094 deduction.

title: Only 2 of 4 estimated payments made
trap: Compute an underpayment penalty for the missed September and January installments, or skip the 2210 analysis.
correct_treatment: Required annual payment = smaller of 90% of 2025 tax ($3,916) or 100% of 2024 tax ($3,159) = $3,159. Withholding is treated as paid evenly; with the April and June $500 payments every cumulative installment is covered -> no penalty, Form 2210 not required.

procedure_section: Return - Schedule A (Medicare premiums from SSA-1099)
title: Medicare Part B/D premiums in the SSA-1099 description
trap: Ignore the Medicare premiums (and Linda's after-tax retiree premiums) when testing itemized deductions, or use net benefits ($35,718) as box 5.
correct_treatment: Box 5 is gross $38,400 (premiums are included in benefits). Medicare B $2,220 + D $462 and the $3,960 after-tax retiree premium go to medical on the Schedule A comparison; after the 7.5% floor, itemized total still < standard deduction -> standard.

title: Canadian pension in CAD
trap: Enter CAD 24,000 as USD, omit it (thinking the treaty/Canadian tax covers it), or leave it out of the taxable SS computation.
correct_treatment: Convert at the IRS 2025 yearly average (1.398): $17,167 on lines 5a/5b; it is included in provisional income for taxable SS (85% maximum reached).

title: FTC on the Canadian pension: general category, no de minimis election
trap: Claim the $2,575 directly on Schedule 3 without Form 1116, or classify as passive.
correct_treatment: Pension is general-category income and not 'qualified passive income' reported on a payee statement, and $2,575 > $600 -> Form 1116 required. Limitation $1,183; credit $1,183; $1,392 added to the carryforward (total $3,860).

title: RBC chequing account -> FBAR + Schedule B Part III
trap: Answer Schedule B line 7a 'No' (the interest is tiny) and skip FBAR, or file Form 8938.
correct_treatment: Max value CAD 37,912 = ~$27,653 (Treasury 12/31 rate) > $10,000 -> FinCEN 114 by Linda (due 4/15, auto-extended to 10/15); Schedule B Part III Yes / Canada; RBC interest is taxable. Form 8938 not required (below MFJ thresholds).

title: Accrued interest paid at purchase
trap: Report box 1 interest as shown ($2,431), or treat tax-exempt interest as taxable / omit it.
correct_treatment: Subtract $386 'Accrued interest' on Schedule B (bond bought between coupon dates). Muni interest $3,115 on line 2a (not taxable, but counts in SS provisional income).

title: Schwab IRA year-end statement in the PBC
trap: Autoflow the IRA's dividends ($9,812), interest ($3,105) and gains ($14,280) onto Schedules B/D.
correct_treatment: Income inside a traditional IRA is not reported; only distributions (1099-R) are taxable.

procedure_section: Scan - Duplicate documents (corrected 1099-R) / QCD age test
title: 'QCD' by a 67-year-old; corrected 1099-R
trap: Use both 1099-Rs (double count $30,000) and/or exclude $8,000 as a QCD per the client and the original code Y.
correct_treatment: Use the CORRECTED 1099-R only. A QCD requires the owner to be 70 1/2 on the distribution date (Robert: 11/14/2028). The full $30,000 is taxable (4b); the $8,000 is a cash charitable contribution usable only if itemizing (it isn't beneficial). No RMD was required (RMD age 73).

procedure_section: Return - Schedule 1-A senior deduction / standard deduction age test
title: Linda is 64 at 12/31/2025
trap: Check both age-65 boxes (+$3,200) and claim the $6,000 senior deduction for both spouses (client says 'Linda is 65 this year').
correct_treatment: Linda turns 65 on 03/22/2026 -> only Robert gets the $1,600 additional standard deduction and the $6,000 senior deduction (MAGI $115,341 < $150,000, no phase-out).

title: Estimates + prior-year overpayment
trap: Enter only the four $1,500 payments (or the organizer's $950 PY figure).
correct_treatment: Line 26 = 4 x $1,500 + $1,150 2024 overpayment applied (per PY return) = $7,150.

title: Two employers -> excess SS withheld
trap: Ignore the excess because each W-2 is correct on its own.
correct_treatment: SS withheld 13,798.34 exceeds $10,918.20 (6.2% x $176,100) -> $2,880 refundable credit on Schedule 3 line 11.

title: Additional Medicare Tax not withheld by either employer
trap: No Form 8959 because neither W-2 shows extra Medicare withholding (each employer paid < $200k).
correct_treatment: Combined Medicare wages 222,553.85 - $200,000 = excess x 0.9% = $203 on Schedule 2. Also NIIT on the Ally interest ($7) since MAGI > $200,000 (the conversion is not NII but raises MAGI).

procedure_section: Review - Client IRAs / General Return Prep Notes (organizer answers vs PY WP)
title: Backdoor Roth with an existing rollover IRA - pro-rata rule
trap: Accept the organizer answer 'no other IRAs' and the planner's 'tax-free' comment: taxable conversion = $12 (earnings only).
correct_treatment: The Fidelity year-end report / 5498 (and the PY WP) show a Rollover IRA worth 63,412.77 at 12/31/2025. Form 8606 line 6 includes it: nontaxable ratio 0.0994 -> taxable conversion $6,315 (line 4b), basis $6,303 carried forward.

title: Remaining IRA basis must be carried forward
trap: Report 8606 Part II only and lose the unrecovered basis.
correct_treatment: File Form 8606 Part I: 2026 basis $6,303. Advise rolling the Rollover IRA into Lakeshore's 401(k) (if the plan accepts roll-ins) before 12/31/2026 to make future backdoor conversions clean.

title: Move Detroit -> Royal Oak creates a part-year Detroit return
trap: File a Detroit resident return as in the prior year (full-year wages at 2.4%), or file nothing because she now lives in Royal Oak.
correct_treatment: Change in residence mid-year -> City of Detroit PART-YEAR resident return: resident-period income at 2.4%; nonresident period only Detroit-source income (none). Royal Oak/Southfield have no city income tax.

procedure_section: SALT Implications - Local Filing Requirements (W-2 box 18-20)
title: Detroit withholding on job-2 wages after the move
trap: Treat Lakeshore's W-2 box 18 Detroit wages ($41,654) as Detroit-taxable, or ignore the Lakeshore box 19 withholding.
correct_treatment: Wages earned 07/01-09/15 as a nonresident working in Southfield/home are not Detroit income; the Detroit tax withheld on them is claimed as a payment on the part-year return and refunded.

procedure_section: SALT Implications - Local Filing Requirements (part-year allocation)
title: Job-2 wages earned while still a Detroit resident
trap: Exclude all Lakeshore wages from Detroit because the job is in Southfield.
correct_treatment: The 06/23-06/30 paycheck (4,153.85, paid 06/30) was earned and received while a Detroit resident -> taxable at the resident rate regardless of work location.

title: MI-1040 treatment
trap: Subtract the Roth conversion (retirement subtraction) or deduct/credit the Detroit tax; or deduct moving expenses.
correct_treatment: MI starts from federal AGI; conversion taxable in MI; exemption $5,800; tax 4.25% = $8,490; no credit for city tax. Moving expenses are not deductible (suspended except Armed Forces).

title: ADP reprint of the job-1 W-2
trap: Autoflow both copies of the Motor City Analytics W-2 (wages, withholding and the excess-SS computation all doubled).
correct_treatment: Same control number / amounts - mark DUP; one W-2 per employer.

procedure_section: Schedule C - Accrual Basis books that should be on cash basis; AJEs
title: QuickBooks P&L is accrual; PY AJE never posted
trap: Enter QuickBooks revenue $186,400 as gross receipts (includes the $9,800 A/R increase, e.g. the December HOA invoice collected 01/2026); or 'fix' tax depreciation to match the unposted books.
correct_treatment: Tax return is cash basis (method used since 2016): gross receipts = revenue - increase in A/R = $176,600 (A/P nil). PY AJE #1 (2024 depreciation 8,486) was not posted, so QB retained earnings/accumulated depreciation do not roll to our PY workpaper - no return impact (tax depreciation comes from our Form 4562 schedule); re-send AJE to bookkeeper.

procedure_section: Schedule C - Book-Tax Differences (meals, personal expenses, club dues, gifts)
title: Personal and limited items buried in the books
trap: Take the QuickBooks expense accounts at face value.
correct_treatment: Remove country club dues $4,200 (sec. 274(a)(3)), Netflix $276, kids' soccer $640, 3 of 4 family phone lines $1,710; meals 50% ($1,570 allowed); gifts limited to $25 x 12 recipients = $300 (sec. 274(b)); truck expenses 85% business.
impact: Sch C expenses overstated ~$10,000 if missed

procedure_section: Schedule C - De-Minimis Safe Harbor Election
title: Mower under $2,500 vs used trailer
trap: Capitalize the $2,300 mower on Form 4562 (or expense it without the election statement); expense the $6,500 trailer as a 'small tool', or depreciate it over 5 years without bonus.
correct_treatment: Mower: de minimis safe harbor (Reg. 1.263(a)-1(f)) - expense on Sch C and attach the annual election statement. Trailer: used 5-year property acquired 03/22/2025 (after 01/19/2025) -> 100% bonus depreciation (automatic; chosen over sec. 179, which needs an election and is income-limited) on Form 4562 Part II. Truck: remaining MACRS from PERM schedule at 85%.
impact: Timing; missing election statement = no safe harbor

procedure_section: Schedule C - Checking the top of Schedule C boxes (Form 1099 filed?)
title: Helpers paid $8,000 and $4,500 by Zelle
trap: Answer line I 'Yes' and line J 'No' (red flag) or 'Yes' without filing; ignore the filing obligation.
correct_treatment: Advise client, obtain W-9s, file late 1099-NECs (filed via IRIS 09/18/2026; penalty exposure up to $340 per form under sec. 6721 plus $340 per payee statement under sec. 6722 for 2026-due returns - Rev. Proc. 2024-40 amounts), then answer I Yes / J Yes.

title: PY prep fee paid personally in 2025
trap: Omit it (not in the books) or deduct the full $1,650 on Schedule C.
correct_treatment: Prorate by time: 1 of 3 hours on Sch C -> $550 to Sch C line 17 legal & professional; the personal 2/3 is nondeductible (misc. itemized deductions eliminated).

procedure_section: Schedule C - SEP IRA (compute maximum amount)
title: SEP computed at 25% of net profit
trap: Deduct 25% x net profit = $21,006 (the employee rate) - creates an excess contribution.
correct_treatment: Self-employed rate is 20% of (net profit - 1/2 SE tax): 20% x $78,089 = $15,618; funded 09/22/2026 before the extended due date. QBI is reduced by the SEP deduction and 1/2 SE tax.

procedure_section: Schedule C - S/E Health Insurance Deduction
title: Spouse's employer offers subsidized family coverage
trap: Deduct the $14,400 BCBS premiums on Sch 1 line 17 (or leave them in Sch C expenses as QuickBooks shows).
correct_treatment: Carlos was eligible to participate in Mission Creek ISD's subsidized plan through Maria (district contributes to every tier) -> sec. 162(l)(2)(B) bars the deduction for all 12 months even though he declined. Premiums go to Schedule A medical, but itemized ($29,989) < standard ($31,500) -> no benefit.

procedure_section: Scan - documents belonging to someone else; Dependents (qualifying relative)
title: Rosa's SSA-1099 and 1099-INT in the PBC
trap: Autoflow adds Rosa's $14,200 SSA-1099 and $85 interest to the Mendozas' return; or omit Rosa as a dependent because 'her SS is more than $5,200'.
correct_treatment: Remove Rosa's documents from the return. Rosa is a qualifying relative: nontaxable Social Security is not gross income (gross income $85 < $5,200), Mendozas provide ~68% of support -> $500 credit for other dependents.

title: Teacher's aide with $410 of receipts
trap: Deduct $410, or deny because she is 'not a teacher'.
correct_treatment: K-12 instructional aide with 900+ hours qualifies (sec. 62(d)(1)); deduction limited to $300.

procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - Debt Basis vs Stock Basis Distribution Trap
title: Distributions exceed STOCK basis; debt basis is positive
trap: Look at total basis (stock $338,640 + debt $120,000) and treat the $360,000 distribution as tax-free.
correct_treatment: Distributions reduce stock basis only. Stock basis before distributions $338,640 -> $21,360 is gain from the sale of stock (sec. 1368(b)(2)) - Form 8949 Part II box F, long-term; Form 7203 attached. Debt basis absorbs only the nondeductible expenses/charitable items (debt basis EOY $114,900).

title: IL PTE tax on the K-1-P
trap: Add the $16,073 PTE tax paid by the corporation to Schedule A line 5a as state income tax, and/or ignore the IL credit.
correct_treatment: The PTE tax was deducted by the corporation (ordinary income is already net of it) - it is not the shareholder's itemized tax. Claim the $16,073 credit on the IL-1040 (Schedule K-1-P); no IL subtraction.
impact: Sch A overstated / IL refund understated

procedure_section: Schedule A - itemizing SALT (refund of taxes itemized in the prior year)
title: 1099-G $2,100 IL refund
trap: Report the $2,100 on Schedule 1 line 1 because she itemized in 2024.
correct_treatment: 2024 SALT was capped at $10,000 with $31,000 paid; without the overpayment she would still have been capped -> no tax benefit -> $0 taxable (tax benefit rule, Rev. Rul. 2019-11). Keep the worksheet.

title: MAGI above $500,000
trap: Deduct the full $40,000 cap (or $32,350 paid), and include the 01/15/2026 IL estimate.
correct_treatment: Cap = 40,000 - 30% x ($552,750 - 500,000) = $24,175. Only IL payments made in 2025 count (withholding + 3 estimates); total paid $32,350 -> limited to $24,175.

procedure_section: Schedule A - Charitable Contributions (DAF vs GoFundMe; noncash clothing)
title: Three kinds of 'donations'
trap: Deduct GoFundMe $1,500 and value clothing at 3x cost per the procedure ($1,800) or at cost ($600).
correct_treatment: DAF $25,000 deductible in 2025 (public charity, written acknowledgment). GoFundMe for a colleague's family is a gift to individuals - not deductible. Used clothing is limited to FMV (thrift value) ~$150 - the procedure's 3x-cost rule conflicts with sec. 170 (FMV of used clothing cannot exceed its cost) and is not followed.
impact: Sch A line 11/12 overstated $3,150 if wrong

procedure_section: Review - Hand-off / estimated payments (organizer vs. confirmation)
title: Organizer says 4 x $15,000 federal estimates
trap: Enter $60,000 on line 26 from the organizer -> understated balance due, IRS math-error notice, no 2210.
correct_treatment: IRS account shows 3 payments ($45,000; Q3 missed). Line 26 = $45,000. 90% of 2025 tax < 110% of 2024 tax -> required annual payment $120,006; Form 2210 regular method penalty $779 (line 38).

title: Medical practice S corp with $612k of W-2 wages
trap: Claim 20% x $310,000 = $62,000 because the W-2 wage limit is met.
correct_treatment: Health is an SSTB; taxable income before QBI is above $247,300 (single) -> applicable percentage 0% -> QBI deduction $0.

title: Excess-distribution gain and K-1 income on Form 8960
trap: Include the K-1 ordinary income and/or the $21,360 excess-distribution gain in NII.
correct_treatment: K-1 income is nonpassive trade/business income (material participation) - not NII. The excess-distribution gain is treated as gain on S-corp stock and removed on line 5c to the extent attributable to the active business (sec. 1411(c)(4), Prop. Reg. 1.1411-7; all corporate assets used in the practice). NII = interest + dividends $4,890 -> NIIT $186.

procedure_section: Scan - duplicate documents (draft vs final K-1)
title: DRAFT K-1 received before the final
trap: Autoflow both K-1s, or use the draft ($326,100 box 1 - before the PTE tax deduction).
correct_treatment: Use only the FINAL K-1 (box 1 $310,000); bookmark the draft as superseded.

procedure_section: Review - Kid Taxes and Filings (separate client ID / project code)
title: Ethan cannot go on Form 8814
trap: Follow the client's request / PY return and report Ethan's $6,400 UTMA income on the parents' return via Form 8814.
correct_treatment: Form 8814 is available only if the child's income is solely interest and dividends (incl. capital gain distributions) and < $13,500. Ethan has a $3,100 capital gain from a fund SALE and $3,200 of wages -> not eligible. Unearned income $6,400 > $2,700 -> Form 8615 on Ethan's own return. Separate client ID EVG1021 and 1040 project code opened.
impact: Parents' return must show nothing for Ethan; Ethan's return EVG1021 carries the kiddie tax

title: Chloe's $1,900 interest - Form 8814 election
trap: Either ignore Chloe's 1099-INT (below $2,700 so 'nothing to report') or add $1,900 to the parents' interest income.
correct_treatment: Chloe must file (unearned > $1,350) unless parents elect Form 8814. Elected: line 4 $1,900 < $2,700 base -> $0 added to parents' income; tax 10% x ($1,900 - $1,350) = $55 added to Form 1040 line 16. Trade-off: identical tax to a separate return for Chloe, one fewer return and fee; no AGI-based items of the parents are affected because $0 is included.

procedure_section: Schedule D - missing cost basis on Consolidated 1099 (equity comp)
title: RSU shares reported with $0 basis
trap: Autoflow takes the 1099-B basis of $0 -> $69,338 of proceeds taxed as gain (the $86,400 of 2025 vest income and the 2023 lot income were already taxed as W-2 wages).
correct_treatment: Form 8949 box B (short-term) / box E (long-term) - basis not reported to IRS; enter 1099-B basis $0, code B, and a negative column (g) adjustment equal to FMV at vest from the supplemental statement. Net RSU gain $9,458 (ST $788, LT $8,670).

procedure_section: Scan - unstructured documents / Payment-app export (household employee)
title: Nanny treated as a 1099 contractor
trap: Accept the client's 1099-NEC treatment (or ignore it - 'not our client's income') and file with no Schedule H.
correct_treatment: Maria is a household employee (family controls when/how the work is done, in their home, their car, weekly pay, no other clients). Cash wages $28,000 >= $2,800 (2025) -> Schedule H: SS/Medicare 15.3% = $4,284; FUTA 0.6% x $7,000 = $42 (WA ESD contributions paid by 04/15/2026) -> $4,326 on Schedule 2 line 9. Obtain EIN, file W-2/W-3 (box 1 includes the $2,142 employee share paid by the employer), file corrected $0 1099-NEC, register with WA ESD; 2024 wages $6,240 also exceeded the 2024 $2,700 threshold -> amend 2024 (separate project).

title: Dependent-care FSA displaces the credit
trap: Claim a $600 credit (20% x $3,000) for Chloe's nanny costs in addition to the $5,000 FSA exclusion.
correct_treatment: Only Chloe (under 13) is a qualifying person (Ethan is 16). With one qualifying person the credit base is $3,000 - $5,000 excluded FSA benefits = $0. Form 2441 is still required (Part III) to support the $5,000 exclusion and list the provider (Maria, SSN).

title: 529 distribution for private K-12 tuition
trap: Treat the $3,123 earnings in box 2 as taxable (no 1098-T), or claim an education credit for the tuition.
correct_treatment: Up to $10,000 per year per beneficiary of K-12 tuition is a qualified expense for 2025 (the $20,000 limit starts 2026). Distribution $10,000 = qualified tuition -> $0 taxable; nothing on the 1040. K-12 tuition is not eligible for AOTC/LLC.

title: High-income phase-outs and surtaxes
trap: Full $4,400 CTC; skip Form 8959 because the employer 'already withheld Additional Medicare'; skip NIIT.
correct_treatment: CTC reduced $50 per $1,000 of MAGI over $400,000 -> $1,950. Form 8959: combined Medicare wages $463,350 - $250,000 MFJ threshold x 0.9% = $1,920; employer withheld only $1,200 (on Daniel's wages over $200,000) - credited on line 25c. NIIT 3.8% x NII $18,928 = $719.

procedure_section: Schedule A - sales tax vs income tax (no-income-tax state)
title: WA residents: general sales tax election
trap: Enter $0 on line 5a (no state income tax), or add both PFML premiums and sales tax.
correct_treatment: Elect general sales taxes (IRS calculator / Axcess blended-rate option): $3,912 > PFML premiums treated as income tax. Only one of income or sales tax may be itemized. Itemized total exceeds the $31,500 standard deduction.

procedure_section: Schedule D - CoinLedger-provided Forms 8949 vs Consolidated 1099 / 1099-DA
title: 1099-DA and CoinLedger both loaded
trap: Autoflow imports the Coinbase 1099-DA (basis blank -> $0) AND the CoinLedger 8949 -> Coinbase sales counted twice, ~$370,811 of extra gain.
correct_treatment: Use the CoinLedger detail (all wallets) as the 8949 source; do not load the 1099-DA separately. Reconcile CoinLedger's Coinbase proceeds $372,300 less sale fees $1,489 = 1099-DA $370,811; report Coinbase sales in 8949 box H/K (1099-DA received, basis not reported) and MetaMask disposals in box I/L (no 1099-DA).

procedure_section: E-File Rejects - IP PIN changes every year
title: Stale IP PIN
trap: Enter the IP PIN from the January 2025 CP01A in the PBC (for the 2024 return).
correct_treatment: IP PINs are valid for one calendar year. The 2026 CP01A went to his old address; the current IP PIN was retrieved from the IRS Online Account (09/28/2026). Using the old PIN rejects the e-file (IP PIN mismatch reject - IND-181/IND-183 family). Also file Form 8822.
impact: E-file reject; late filing if not caught before 10/15

title: Coinbase 'Send' rows treated as sales
trap: Treat the 3.5 ETH sent to MetaMask as dispositions (or as withdrawals of income).
correct_treatment: Transfers between wallets the taxpayer controls are not taxable; basis and holding period carry over (CoinLedger tracks the 2.0 ETH later swapped on Uniswap with its 04/22/2025 basis).

title: Kraken 1099-MISC double-counted
trap: Report the $1,240 1099-MISC AND the CoinLedger income total $2,100.44 -> $3,340.44.
correct_treatment: CoinLedger's staking total already includes the Kraken rewards. Report $2,100.44 once on Schedule 1 line 8v (ordinary income at FMV when received - Rev. Rul. 2023-14; not SE income for an investor). It is also net investment income.

procedure_section: Schedule D - adjustment codes (C collectibles, W wash sale)
title: Wash sale rule and crypto; NFT collectible
trap: Disallow the $14,866 BTC loss (repurchased 11 days later) as a wash sale; or treat the NFT gain as ordinary 15%/20% LTCG; or ignore Robinhood's 1g wash-sale amount.
correct_treatment: Section 1091 applies to stock or securities - not to digital assets in 2025 -> BTC loss fully allowed. The Robinhood TSLA wash sale (code W, $3,960) IS applied as reported. The NFT is digital art -> collectible (Notice 2023-27 look-through) -> 28% rate gain $8,976 (8949 code C; Sch D line 18).

title: Advance PTC based on $36k projected income
trap: Omit Form 8962 (no 1095-A input) or cap repayment at the table amount.
correct_treatment: Household income $227,890 = 1,513% of FPL. At 8.5% the monthly contribution $1,614 exceeds the SLCSP ($441) -> PTC $0 every month; repay ALL APTC $3,528 (no repayment cap at/above 400% FPL) on Schedule 2 line 2.

title: NIIT limited by MAGI over threshold
trap: 3.8% x all net investment income $206,490 = $7,847; or no NIIT because wages are low.
correct_treatment: NIIT = 3.8% x lesser of NII $206,490 or MAGI over $200,000 ($27,890) = $1,060.

procedure_section: Billing - expedite fee / Investor vs trader
title: Late documents and non-deductible investor costs
trap: Deduct CoinLedger subscription / hardware wallet on Schedule C or Schedule A; skip the 15% expedite fee.
correct_treatment: Investor (not a trader): no Schedule C; investment expenses are miscellaneous itemized deductions - suspended (permanently after OBBBA). Final CoinLedger report received 09/26/2026, within 15 days of 10/15/2026 -> 15% expedited processing fee per engagement letter.

procedure_section: General Return Prep Notes - blank organizer line with PY amount
title: Installment payments missing from the organizer
trap: Organizer installment-sale question and the Caldwell note line are blank -> no 2025 installment income or note interest reported.
correct_treatment: PY return and PERM show a 2024 installment sale with a 10-year note. Blank line is not zero: called June (03/04) and used her ledger + amortization schedule. Report 2025 principal x GP% on Form 6252 and the interest on Schedule B.

title: Recognize gain only on principal received
trap: Report the full $245,600 remaining gain in 2025, or apply GP% to the total checks (principal + interest).
correct_treatment: Gain = principal received in 2025 $23,126 x 73.0952% (GP% from the 2024 6252) = $16,904, long-term (land held since 1998) -> Schedule D line 11. Interest is not a payment on the selling price.

procedure_section: Installment Sales - review the payment schedule dates
title: December payment received in January 2026
trap: Use the amortization schedule's 12 scheduled payments for 2025.
correct_treatment: Cash-basis taxpayers report payments when received. Payment 12 (due 12/15/2025) was received 01/06/2026 -> 2026. 2025 = 11 payments: principal $23,126, interest $17,908.
impact: Gain overstated $1,583 and interest $1,564 if 12 payments used

title: June's ledger mis-splits a payment; late fee
trap: Key the handwritten ledger as-is (March check all 'principal'; total 'rec'd 2025' includes interest).
correct_treatment: Use the attorney amortization schedule for the interest/principal split (payments apply to interest first per the note). The $75 July late charge is additional interest income (Sch B).

title: Buyer name, SSN and address required
trap: Lump the note interest with bank interest or list only 'Caldwell note'.
correct_treatment: Interest on a seller-financed mortgage where the buyer uses the property as a personal residence is listed first on Schedule B line 1 with the buyer's name, address and SSN ($50 penalty for omission).

title: Senior deduction phase-out
trap: Take $12,000 (2 x $6,000) without the MAGI test, or skip it because they take the additional standard deduction.
correct_treatment: Both 65+ -> $6,000 each, reduced by 6% of MAGI over $150,000 ($7,434 x 6% = $446 each) -> $11,108. It is in addition to the standard deduction (incl. 2 x $1,600 age add-ons).

title: NC exclusions for Bailey-vested TSERS and Social Security
trap: Tax June's TSERS pension in NC (or exempt Walter's private pension too); forget the SS subtraction.
correct_treatment: Schedule S: deduct taxable SS $49,317 and June's TSERS benefits $30,788 (5+ years creditable service as of 08/12/1989). Walter's private pension and IRA are taxable in NC. NC taxable income $51,829 x 4.25% = $2,203.

procedure_section: Schedule A - Medicare premiums from SSA-1099
title: Itemized vs standard for seniors
trap: Itemize using the organizer medical total only, or ignore Medicare Part B shown on the SSA-1099s.
correct_treatment: Add Medicare Part B $4,440 from the SSA-1099 descriptions to medical; still, itemized $8,192 < standard $34,700 -> standard deduction.

title: 83(b) election mailed 37 days after grant
trap: Accept the client's Form 15620 at face value: report $8,000 of compensation income for 2025 (Sch 1 / line 1h) and attach the election copy.
correct_treatment: Grant 11/03/2025 -> 30-day deadline 12/03/2025; USPS postmark 12/10/2025. Election is invalid (no relief under Reg. 1.83-2 / no 9100 relief). No 2025 income; income is recognized at each vesting at FMV then. Advise client in writing (and Loomwork counsel re: possible cancel-and-regrant with a new timely election).
impact: Income overstated $8,000 (tax ~$1,920) if reported; future vesting income ignored

procedure_section: Schedule D (missing / incorrect cost basis on consolidated 1099)
title: NSO same-day sale: 1099-B basis = exercise price only
trap: Autoflow the 1099-B as reported: $4,000 basis -> $21,975 short-term gain on top of the $22,000 already in W-2 box 1.
correct_treatment: Form 8949 box A, report 1099-B basis $4,000 in col (e), code B, adjustment ($22,000) -> loss ($25) (commission).

title: E*TRADE Stock Plan Transactions Supplement repeats the 1099-B sale
trap: Enter both the 1099-B and the supplement's 'adjusted gain' line as separate sales (double-counting proceeds).
correct_treatment: The supplement is informational (same transaction). Use it only to support the code B basis adjustment.

title: ISO spread is an AMT adjustment, not regular income
trap: Either (a) ignore Form 3921 (no W-2/1099 income -> no AMT), or (b) add the $50,000 spread to wages.
correct_treatment: Regular tax: nothing. Form 6251 line 2i $50,000 -> AMT $4,346. Track AMT basis $56,000 vs regular $6,000; Form 8801 minimum tax credit carryforward $4,346 to 2026 (deferral item).

title: HSA code W already equals the self-only limit; extra $1,000 is excess
trap: Deduct the $1,000 direct contribution on Schedule 1 line 13 (or deduct $5,300 per 5498-SA).
correct_treatment: Limit $4,300 - code W $4,300 = $0 deduction. Excess $1,000 + $38 earnings withdrawn 09/15/2026, before the 10/15/2026 extended due date -> no 6% excise (no Form 5329); $38 earnings taxable in 2026, not 2025. File 8889.
impact: Adjustments overstated $1,000; or $60 excise wrongly assessed

procedure_section: General Return Prep Notes / estimated tax (Form 2210)
title: AMT creates a balance due - is there a penalty?
trap: Compute a Form 2210 penalty because withholding < 90% of 2025 tax.
correct_treatment: Withholding $27,600 >= 100% of 2024 tax $23,526 (2024 AGI under $150,000) -> safe harbor met, no penalty. Extension payment $6,000 (Sch 3 line 10) avoids late-payment interest.

title: Illinois has no AMT and taxes the NSO income as wages
trap: Add an IL adjustment for the ISO spread or subtract the NSO income as 'already taxed on 1099-B'.
correct_treatment: IL base income = federal AGI $165,959; exemption $2,850; tax 4.95% = $8,074; refund $76. Chicago has no city income tax.

title: Married 12/20/2025 - co-worker says file Single
trap: File two Single returns because they were married for only 11 days.
correct_treatment: Marital status is determined on 12/31: married for the entire year -> MFJ or MFS only.

title: Client asks for the cheaper of joint / separate
trap: Pick MFS because 'we only just got married', or pick MFJ without modeling.
correct_treatment: Model both: MFJ total tax $12,292 vs MFS combined $14,996 -> MFJ saves $2,704. MI flat tax - no difference. Document the simulation and reconcile to the compliance return.

title: Organizer signed 'Sofia Hart'; SSA still shows Martinez
trap: Enter the primary taxpayer as 'Sofia Hart' per the organizer / client email.
correct_treatment: Use the name on the SSA record (Sofia E. Martinez, name control MART) until she files Form SS-5. Actual history: rejected IND-031-04 on 04/08; document reason, save corrected version, retransmit 04/09, monitor to acceptance 04/10.
impact: E-file reject; possible late filing if not monitored

procedure_section: Scan - duplicate documents / Schedule C records
title: 1099-K (Stripe) includes the $9,500 on the Arbor Brewing 1099-NEC
trap: Gross receipts = 18,000 + 9,500 + 12,400 = $39,900 (all information returns added).
correct_treatment: Reconcile Stripe balance history: $9,500 of the $12,400 is Arbor Brewing card payments. Unique receipts = $18,000 + $12,400 + Venmo $350 (no form - still income) = $30,750. Keep the reconciliation in the WP.
impact: Sch C overstated $9,500 (~$2,900 income + SE tax) or Venmo omitted

procedure_section: Schedule C - Home Office Deduction (8829 vs simplified)
title: Part-year home office in a rented apartment
trap: Use simplified $5 x 150 = $750, or 8829 with 12 months of rent.
correct_treatment: 8829 actual: 16.67% x Apr-Dec rent/utilities/insurance $19,233 = $3,206 vs simplified $563 (average monthly footage 112.5) -> 8829.

procedure_section: Schedule C - checking the top-of-form boxes / De-Minimis Safe Harbor / personal expenses
title: First-year business boxes and personal items in client books
trap: Leave line H blank; depreciate the laptop over 5 years; deduct the wedding invitations and Spotify from the spreadsheet.
correct_treatment: Check line H (started 2025); line I 'No' (no payments requiring 1099s). Attach the de minimis safe harbor election statement (laptop $1,899, tablet $379 <= $2,500). Remove personal items ($739).

title: No estimates on a first-year Schedule C; balance due > $1,000
trap: Assess a 2210 penalty because withholding $9,446 < 90% of 2025 tax $11,063.
correct_treatment: MFJ in 2025 but separate in 2024 -> prior-year safe harbor = Liam $5,963 + Sofia $2,947 = $8,910 <= withholding -> no penalty. Advise 2026 estimates.

title: Unemployment 1099-G with federal and MI withholding
trap: Omit unemployment (client thinks it was 'already taxed') or omit the $546 box 4 withholding.
correct_treatment: Sch 1 line 7 $5,460 (taxable federal and MI); $546 on line 25b; $232 MI withholding on MI-1040.

title: NRE interest is tax-free in India - client never reported it
trap: Omit NRE interest (organizer says 'tax free in India').
correct_treatment: US residents are taxed on worldwide income; the Indian section 10(4)(ii) exemption is irrelevant. Report INR 420,000 / 87.147 = $4,819 on Schedule B. Flag 2024 omission to signer (amend / streamlined).

procedure_section: Foreign Transactions (use IRS rates; foreign-currency amounts)
title: Indian certificates are on the April-March fiscal year
trap: Use the FY 2024-25 certificate totals (INR 400,000 NRE / 173,000 NRO) as 2025 income.
correct_treatment: Build calendar-2025 interest from quarterly credits: Q1 from the FY24-25 certificate + Q2-Q4 from the FY25-26 certificate (NRE INR 420,000; NRO INR 180,000; TDS INR 56,160). Convert at the IRS 2025 average 87.147.

title: TDS withheld at 31.2% but treaty rate on interest is 15%
trap: Claim the full TDS $644 as a credit (as the client did in 2024).
correct_treatment: Only the tax legally owed under the US-India treaty (15%) is a compulsory, creditable tax (Reg. 1.901-2(e)(5)): INR 27,000 = $310. Excess INR 29,160 is refundable from India (ITR + Form 10F/TRC) - not creditable.

title: De minimis election is not available
trap: Foreign tax under $600 MFJ -> claim directly on Schedule 3 without Form 1116 (procedure shortcut).
correct_treatment: The election also requires all foreign income to be passive AND reported on a qualified payee statement (1099-INT/DIV, K-1). Indian bank certificates / Form 16A are not -> Form 1116 (passive) required. Procedure imprecise - law followed.

title: Mutual fund folios omitted; wrong exchange rate
trap: Repeat the 2024 FBAR (4 bank accounts) and convert at the IRS yearly average rate.
correct_treatment: Report all 7 accounts (incl. 3 mutual fund folios - 'other financial accounts') at maximum value converted at the Treasury 12/31/2025 rate (INR 89.87). Aggregate max $202,648. Joint accounts -> one FBAR + Form 114a. Due 10/15/2026 (automatic).

title: FBAR filed so 8938 'not needed'
trap: Skip Form 8938 because the FBAR covers the accounts.
correct_treatment: Separate requirement. MFJ living in US: year-end value $194,843 > $100,000 -> Form 8938 attached to the 1040; PFIC holdings counted toward the threshold and listed as excepted (3 Forms 8621).

title: Indian mutual funds (growth option, no sales) are PFICs
trap: No income, no sale -> nothing to report.
correct_treatment: Each fund is a PFIC. Aggregate value $72,327 > $50,000 MFJ exemption -> annual Form 8621 (Part I, section 1291 fund, no excess distribution) for each of the 3 funds. Recommend MTM (section 1296) discussion; QEF not available.

title: INR 1.3 crore gift from a nonresident-alien parent
trap: Either report it as income, or ignore it because gifts are not taxable.
correct_treatment: Not income, but gifts > $100,000 from a nonresident alien individual require Form 3520 Part IV ($150,813 credited 06/18/2025). Due 10/15/2026 with the extension; mailed separately. Penalty up to 25% of the gift.

title: Parents lived with them 6 months, fully supported
trap: Claim both parents as qualifying relatives ($500 ODC each) and apply for ITINs.
correct_treatment: Dependents must be US citizens, nationals, or residents of the US, Canada or Mexico. Parents are Indian residents; 177 days in the US on B-2 (< 183, no prior-year days) -> nonresident aliens. No ODC. (Additional Medicare $1,233 and NIIT $324 also apply - combined wages > $250,000; NII = all interest incl. foreign.)

title: Divorce final 02/10/2026; client wants 'Single'
trap: File Single because the divorce is final when the return is prepared, or MFS because the agreement says 'separate returns'.
correct_treatment: Marital status is tested at 12/31/2025 - still married. But she is 'considered unmarried' (separate return, paid > half of home costs, child lived with her > half year, spouse out of home last 6 months) -> HOH, which also satisfies the agreement's 'separate returns' clause.
impact: HOH vs MFS: std deduction $23,625 vs $15,750 + brackets + credits

title: Separation agreement: spousal support + child support
trap: Report $13,500 spousal support as alimony income (Sch 1 line 2a) and/or child support as income.
correct_treatment: Instrument executed 03/20/2025 (after 2018) -> alimony is neither income to her nor deductible by Brian. Child support is never income. Nothing reported.

title: Liam released to Brian for 2025 (odd year)
trap: Claim both children for CTC ($4,400), or drop Liam from HOH / Form 2441 as well.
correct_treatment: Form 8332 releases only the dependency-related credits (CTC/ODC). Megan claims CTC for Nora only ($2,200); she remains custodial parent: Liam still counts for HOH and as a Form 2441 qualifying person (and EIC, though not eligible here).

title: QDRO distribution to alternate payee, age 36
trap: Report on line 4 (IRA) and/or assess the 10% additional tax ($3,000) because code 1 is shown.
correct_treatment: Taxable $30,000 on line 5a/5b (qualified plan). File Form 5329 with exception 04 (72(t)(2)(C) - payment to alternate payee under a QDRO) -> $0 additional tax. $6,000 (20%) withheld on line 25b.

procedure_section: OBBBA - no tax on overtime (Schedule 1-A Part III)
title: Employer reported the FLSA premium itself
trap: Divide the box 14 amount by 3 (as for total-OT W-2s like EVG1001), deducting only $1,620.
correct_treatment: Box 14 'QUAL OT PREM' and the employer letter show the premium portion only -> full $4,860 qualifies. Considered-unmarried HOH is not 'married' for 7703 purposes, so the joint-return requirement does not bar the deduction.

title: Michigan exemptions after Form 8332 release
trap: Claim 3 MI exemptions (Megan + both kids) as in the organizer.
correct_treatment: MI personal exemptions follow the dependents claimed on the federal return: Megan + Nora = 2 x $5,800 (assumption stated: Brian claims Liam's MI exemption).

title: Grand Rapids resident city return
trap: No city return (client's ex-spouse's city has none) or omit the QDRO distribution from city income.
correct_treatment: Grand Rapids resident (1.5%) GR-1040R required; premature distribution taxable to the city; tax $1,762 vs withheld $1,311 -> $451 due 04/30/2026.

title: Brian's W-2 uploaded by Megan
trap: Add Brian's W-2 to her return (or prepare a joint return).
correct_treatment: Separate return - Brian's W-2 is not hers; do not import. Keep out of her WP (confidentiality; Brian is not our client).

procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - S corp IRC 311(b) property distribution
title: S corp omitted the 311(b) gain on the truck
trap: Enter the K-1 as issued: box 1 $62,000, property distribution at book value $12,000 -> no gain.
correct_treatment: Distribution of appreciated property = deemed sale at FMV at the corporate level (IRC 311(b), 1371(a)). Gain $20,000 (FMV $32,000 - adjusted basis $12,000) is all IRC 1245 recapture (accumulated depreciation $33,000) -> ordinary, flows through box 1. Manually add to the K-1 ordinary income: $82,000.

procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - basis limitation (Section 5 line 16 other increases)
title: Basis ordering with a property distribution
trap: Reduce basis by the book value (or reduce by FMV without first adding the gain) -> wrong ending basis, or a phantom excess-distribution capital gain.
correct_treatment: Form 7203: increase stock basis by the gain first, then reduce by distributions at FMV ($72,000); basis before distributions $178,150 is sufficient -> no capital gain; ending basis $101,750. Elena's basis in the truck = FMV $32,000 (IRC 301(d)).

procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - S corp accountant fails to reflect 311(b); Review - tax research
title: Reporting inconsistently with the K-1 requires Form 8082
trap: Silently report different numbers from the K-1 (IRS matching / IRC 6037(c) consistency) or wait for an amended K-1 past the extended due date.
correct_treatment: Attach Form 8082 (inconsistent treatment) identifying box 1 and box 16D differences; notify the S corp's CPA to amend the 1120-S (agreed 09/02/2026). Keep the email in the WP.

procedure_section: QBI - ensure QBI, UBIA and W-2 wages properly reported
title: QBI includes the 1245 recapture; reduced by SE health
trap: Use K-1 Statement A QBI of $62,000 (omits gain), or exclude the gain as 'not QBI', or ignore the health-insurance reduction.
correct_treatment: IRC 1245 recapture is ordinary trade-or-business income -> QBI. QBI = $82,000 - $7,800 2% shareholder health deduction = $74,200; taxable income below $197,300 -> 20% = $14,840; W-2 wages/UBIA not limiting.

title: 2% shareholder health insurance
trap: Treat the $7,800 in box 1 as ordinary wages with no deduction (or deduct it on Schedule A medical).
correct_treatment: Premiums paid by the S corp for a >2% shareholder are included in W-2 box 1 (not boxes 3/5) and deductible on Sch 1 line 17 (Notice 2008-1), limited to the S corp wages.

procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - trust termination suspended passive losses
title: Trust's $18,400 suspended PAL on the distributed condo
trap: Deduct the $18,400 suspended loss on Schedule E (Hector: 'you might be able to use them').
correct_treatment: IRC 469(j)(12): on distribution of the passive activity the losses are never deductible; they increase the basis of the distributed property. Condo basis $222,546 + $18,400 = $240,946 (carryover basis under IRC 643(e), no 643(e)(3) election). Record in PERM for 2026 depreciation.

title: Trust's long-term capital loss carryover passes to beneficiary
trap: Ignore box 11 code E (not on 1099s) or treat it as a current-year K-1 loss.
correct_treatment: Final K-1 box 11 code E $3,200 -> Schedule D line 14 in the beneficiary's year the trust terminates (Reg. 1.642(h)-1). Net capital loss limited to $3,000; $200 carries to 2026.

procedure_section: Scan - duplicate documents (draft vs final K-1)
title: Draft trust K-1 in the PBC
trap: Load both the June DRAFT and August FINAL trust K-1s (double interest/dividends), or use the draft's $410 interest.
correct_treatment: Use only the FINAL K-1 (interest $420). Bookmark the draft as superseded.

title: No 2025 Schedule E for the inherited-then-distributed condo
trap: Start depreciation in 2025 on stepped-up or FMV basis ($305,000), or claim the trust's 2025 depreciation again.
correct_treatment: Not held out for rent in 2025 (painting; listed March 2026) -> no 2025 Sch E. 2026: continue trust's 27.5-yr schedule on carryover building basis $174,546 (IRC 168(i)(7)); the $14,431 basis increase is treated as a new 27.5-yr asset (assumption). Holding period tacks.

procedure_section: Schedule E / Rental Properties; Scan - Schedule E records (hours log)
title: Short-term rental: not a 'rental activity'; material participation
trap: Treat the Airbnb condo as a passive rental: loss suspended on Form 8582 (MAGI < $100k -> maybe $25k allowance) or move it to Schedule C with SE tax.
correct_treatment: Average stay 3.10 nights (<= 7) -> not a rental activity (Reg. 1.469-1T(e)(3)(ii)(A)); no substantial services -> stays on Schedule E (no SE tax). Handwritten log: 180 hours, more than any other individual (cleaner ~95) -> material participation test 3 -> nonpassive. Loss ($15,147) offsets wages; no Form 8582.
impact: Sch 1 line 5 ($15,147); tax effect ~22% of the loss

title: Airbnb 1099-K gross vs payouts vs occupancy taxes
trap: Report the organizer's payout figure $48,447 (and still deduct host fees = double deduction), or treat the occupancy/sales tax column as income and a deduction.
correct_treatment: Rents = 1099-K gross $49,945 (nightly + cleaning fees), host fees $1,498 deducted once; occupancy/sales taxes $6,368 collected and remitted by Airbnb are neither income nor deductible. Reconciled CSV to 1099-K.

procedure_section: Schedule E / Rental Properties - personal use days
title: Personal-use days: 280A allocation, not the vacation-home limit
trap: Ignore the girls' trip (deduct 100% of all expenses) or treat the condo as a vacation home and limit expenses to income.
correct_treatment: 6 personal days < greater of 14 / 10% of 192 -> not a residence; shared expenses x 192/198. Personal share of property tax ($66) to Sch A; personal share of mortgage interest ($429) is nondeductible personal interest (condo not a qualified residence). Maintenance days are not personal days.
impact: Sch E expenses; Sch A line 5b

procedure_section: Schedule E / Rental Properties - capitalization of repairs; Scan - spreadsheet
title: Client spreadsheet expenses closing costs, furniture and personal items
trap: Deduct the spreadsheet as-is: closing costs, $24.6k furniture as 'supplies', full property-tax bill, occupancy taxes, Dollywood pass, gas receipts.
correct_treatment: Capitalize acquisition costs into basis ($388,410; land $58,262 per assessor ratio); building 39-yr MM (unit used on a transient basis is not a 'dwelling unit' for 27.5-yr); furniture 5-yr with 100% bonus (acquired after 01/19/2025) on Form 4562; loan costs amortized; property tax limited to her post-closing share $2,163 (IRC 164(d)); mileage at 70c replaces gas; Dollywood pass is personal.

title: Gambling: gross winnings, losses capped, 2025 = 100%
trap: Net the jackpot against losses and report nothing (client's view), or deduct $15,400, or apply the OBBBA 90% limit (procedure text says 'in effect for 2026').
correct_treatment: Report $12,000 W-2G winnings on Sch 1 line 8b; losses deductible only as an itemized deduction (Sch A line 16) limited to winnings = $12,000. The 90% limit applies to tax years beginning after 12/31/2025 - not 2025. Procedure wording is imprecise; law followed.

procedure_section: Schedule A - itemize vs standard / sales tax
title: Itemizing only works because of the gambling losses
trap: Take the standard deduction (as in 2024) - losing the gambling-loss deduction and taxing $12,000 of winnings in full.
correct_treatment: Itemized $23,992 (sales tax - TN has no income tax - + real estate tax + home mortgage + charity + gambling) vs standard $15,750; without gambling itemized would be $11,992.

procedure_section: Schedule A - Disaster Losses (federally declared only)
title: Windstorm tree damage is not deductible
trap: Deduct the $1,000 deductible and $2,400 tree removal as a casualty loss.
correct_treatment: Personal casualty losses for 2025 are deductible only if attributable to a federally declared disaster (Form 4684); the 07/18/2025 storm had no declaration (insurer letter). Expansion to state-declared disasters starts 2026. $0; no gain because reimbursement did not exceed basis.

title: NC nonresident return for NC-casino winnings
trap: No state return because Tennessee has no income tax; the $510 NC withholding is lost (or claimed on the 1040).
correct_treatment: Winnings from a North Carolina casino are NC-source; file D-400 as nonresident with Schedule PN: NC taxable income x 0.1347 -> tax $437 vs withholding $510 -> refund $73. NC does not allow gambling losses.

procedure_section: Review - Kid Taxes and Filings (separate client ID / project code)
title: Child needs his own return
trap: Report Ethan's income on the parents' Form 8814 like 2024, or skip his return because 'he's a dependent'.
correct_treatment: Capital gain from a sale + wages -> Form 8814 not allowed. Unearned income $6,400 > $1,350 filing threshold and > $2,700 kiddie threshold -> separate Form 1040 with Form 8615, under its own client ID (EVG1021) and 1040 project code, after discussing with parents.

procedure_section: Kid Taxes - Form 8615 using parents' return
title: Parents' rate from the FINAL parents' return
trap: Tax all of Ethan's income at his own 10%/0% rates, or use an estimated/prior-year parent taxable income.
correct_treatment: Form 8615 line 6 = parents' 2025 taxable income $402,319 (EVG1010, MFJ); line 10 = parents' tax $80,830 excluding the $55 Form 8814 tax. NUI $3,700 taxed at the parents' marginal rates -> $628. If the parents' return changes (amended), Ethan's return must be amended too.

title: Preferential rates keep applying inside Form 8615
trap: Tax the whole $3,700 of NUI at the parents' top bracket (their taxable income is in the 32% bracket).
correct_treatment: The share of qualified dividends (1,098.44) and capital gain (1,792.19) included in NUI (line 5 / line 1) is taxed at the parents' 15% capital gain rate on line 9. The ordinary part is taxed at 24%, not 32%: the parents' ORDINARY income (TI less QD/CG = $386,538) is in the 24% bracket because the QDCG worksheet stacks QD/CG on top. The rest of the child's QD/CG is taxed at his own 0% rate on line 15.
impact: Line 11 $628 vs $1,184 if all NUI at 32%

title: Dependent standard deduction
trap: Use the full $15,750 single standard deduction (-> $0 taxable income), or the $1,350 minimum ignoring wages.
correct_treatment: Dependent: greater of $1,350 or earned income + $450 = $3,650 (capped at $15,750). Taxable income $5,950.

title: Only unearned income is subject to kiddie tax
trap: Include the $3,200 lifeguard wages in Form 8615 line 1.
correct_treatment: Line 1 = unearned income only ($900 + $2,400 + $3,100 = $6,400). Wages are taxed at the child's own rates (line 14/15).

title: Dependent checkbox / no credits for the child
trap: Leave the 'can be claimed as a dependent' box unchecked, or claim his own personal credits.
correct_treatment: Check the box on page 1 (the parents claim him and the CTC). No CTC/EITC on his return; Form 8615 lists the parent's name/SSN. Balance due $642 < $1,000 and no 2024 liability -> no Form 2210.
